summary: Perimeter IDS/IPS reassembly timeout intermittently drops long-lived gRPC/TLS streams to private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusPay reports intermittent gRPC streaming disconnects from their private deployment. Streams fail after variable durations (10s-90s) with TCP RSTs observed at the customer perimeter. Impact: production request failures for streaming responses (chat and streaming codegen), increased user-visible timeouts and retries.

Impact:
- ~8% of streaming sessions to their dedicated private cluster are failing intermittently during business hours (estimated 2-3k streams/day).
- Non-streaming (short request) paths appear unaffected.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering) in us-east-1, customer-managed perimeter firewall with IDS/IPS and TLS inspection enabled.
- Redwood control plane communicates to customer agents over TLS 1.3 gRPC; model pulls use the same path.
- Affected services: streaming generation endpoints, realtime chat websocket fallback paths.

Steps to reproduce (observed reliably in lab with customer config):
1) Establish long-lived gRPC bidi stream to the model endpoint and periodically send/receive frames larger than 8 KB.
2) Let stream run for 30-90s under realistic token emission patterns.
3) Observe abrupt stream closure with server-side write failures and client-side TCP RST.

Observed behavior:
- TCP RST bursts from the customer perimeter (seen in VPC flow logs and customer firewall logs).
- IDS/IPS alerts correlate with fragmented/reassembled TLS application data exceeding the device's reassembly window or hitting an internal reassembly timeout.
- When TLS inspection is disabled on the perimeter, the issue disappears.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived TLS/gRPC streams should remain stable across customer perimeter when not actively blocked. TLS inspection should not cause opaque stream resets.

Attachments/links:
- Customer-provided pcap snippets (redacted) showing RST after sequence of PUSH/ACKs.
- VPC flow logs and firewall alert IDS IDs (included in logs field below).

Recommended immediate workaround:
- For customer: disable TLS inspection for traffic between their perimeter and Redwood endpoints (or create an allow/whitelist rule for control-plane/model IPs) until a long-term change is in place.
- For Redwood: deliver guidance on switching to the hosted-control-plane via PrivateLink or pinning a dedicated, non-inspected endpoint as an option for streaming-heavy workloads.

investigation_notes: 03/10 15:05 - Talked with NimbusPay network team (Marco Reyes). They confirmed perimeter appliance performs TLS inspection and has an IDS reassembly window of ~60s and max reassembly buffer of 16KB.
03/10 16:20 - Reproduced in customer lab by enabling TLS inspection on a lab appliance running same FW/IPS signatures. Disabling TLS inspection prevented resets.

03/11 09:12 - Hypothesis: appliance attempts TLS stream reassembly for inspection, but large/variable gRPC frames + TCP segmentation cause the IPS reassembly engine to drop and send TCP RSTs or terminate session on timeout.

03/11 11:30 - Correlated with rule set v5.2.4 on perimeter (see IDS signature 81827). Rule triggers when application payload reassembly exceeds device timeout or buffer; appliance may opt to reset connection to avoid resource exhaustion.
03/12 10:00 - Eng ran a controlled test with reduced max gRPC frame size and keepalive frequency, observed fewer resets but still occasional failures under high token emission bursts.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:30 - Marco Reyes (NimbusPay): 'We see the same RSTs in our perimeter. Going to test disabling TLS inspection for traffic to Redwood tomorrow morning.'
2026-03-10 16:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): 'Thanks Marco—can you share firewall model and rule set? Also capture pcap around RSTs if possible.'

2026-03-11 11:45 - Lena Chen (SRE): 'We can recommend two customer-side mitigations: 1) mark control-plane/model IPs as exempt from TLS inspection; 2) increase reassembly buffers/timeouts in IPS. We're also exploring Redwood-side mitigations.'
2026-03-12 09:20 - NimbusPay: 'Disabling TLS inspection for the prefix eliminated failures in preliminary test. We'll plan a controlled rollout during maintenance window.'
resolution: Immediate mitigation applied by customer: disabled TLS inspection for Redwood control-plane/model prefixes. Observed elimination of stream resets in canary traffic (03/12 rollout).

Temporary Redwood mitigation: engineering suggested reducing default gRPC max frame size for private deployments as a configuration option to avoid large single-frame emissions (follow-up PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482).

Long term: document recommended network config for private deployments that includes either TLS bypass for control-plane/model egress or explicit allowlists for streaming heavy traffic. Create KB article for customers running perimeter TLS inspection appliances describing signatures to tune and suggested reassembly/timeouts.

Follow-up action: Coordinate with NimbusPay to validate production for 72 hours then close ticket. If customer cannot disable TLS inspection, SRE to work with product on an opt-in TLS-termination handshake option or PrivateLink path to bypass customer IPS.
